source_contract.second_class_scope_rule: All reviewed Chapter 4 locators are outside subsections explicitly marked 〔一等〕; first-class-only 4.3.5 and Category III radio calculations remain excluded.

review_basis: B8 within-batch collision notes and nearest canonical neighbors
current official MLIT 教則第5版 Chapter 4 source contract
answer correctness, answer uniqueness, distractor plausibility, commercial practice value, proposition/misconception/reasoning-path distinctness

decisions.rationale: 4.1 explicitly notes that fixed-wing automated takeoff/landing may require launcher/recovery ground equipment. Existing fixed-wing items test minimum speed, glide and control surfaces, not ground-equipment requirements.

Tier B PASS. The source-defined large-helicopter hover branch changes both aircraft applicability and control timing: large inertia delays response, so early control is required. Q099 tests generic large-aircraft acceleration/deceleration and obstacle avoidance, not hover anticipation.

The source-defined safety consequence of fixed-wing glide is a broadened possible impact/forced-landing area. Q144 tests glide capability itself; this item tests the distinct hazard implication for impact-location estimation.

The item tests the definition/sign convention of aerodynamic angle of attack and sideslip from relative airflow. Existing items test stall at high angle of attack or attitude angles, not these definitions.

The source states that many FCS sensors require aircraft-specific calibration. Q043 is the narrower geomagnetic-sensor calibration case, so the system-level calibration discipline is a separate proposition rather than a wording variant.
The transmitter role includes outbound commands and, in some systems, inbound aircraft information. Q004 covers the outbound command path; the telemetry-reception direction is materially distinct.

The source explicitly links low remaining LiPo voltage to abrupt output weakening and possible crash. Existing low-voltage/current/failsafe items do not directly test this end-of-charge output-collapse proposition.
General radio-wave interference can strengthen or weaken a combined signal. Existing diffraction/multipath items do not directly test the general interference proposition.

The distance-squared attenuation relationship is explicit second-class-applicable Chapter 4 material and is not the excluded Category III calculation material. The simple 2x-distance -> 1/4 power-density application is answer-unique and practice-relevant.
Water absorption causing substantial radio attenuation is an explicit propagation-medium proposition absent from the current canonical diffraction/multipath coverage.

Tier B PASS. Q075 tests multipath mechanism/result; this item tests the source-defined recovery action after control degradation—raise transmitter position and change antenna orientation—so response sequence and reasoning path are materially different.

The source gives distinct positioning accuracy classes for standalone GPS versus RTK/DGPS. Existing GNSS items test satellite count or the need for high-accuracy positioning, not this architecture-to-accuracy comparison.

The item tests preventive GNSS-receiver installation considering terrain/obstacles. Existing GNSS questions test operational effects such as multipath or waypoint error, not installation-site selection.

The source explicitly states that GNSS vertical error is generally larger than horizontal error. This directional accuracy limitation is distinct from existing cause/effect and high-precision-positioning questions.

Tier B PASS. Q072 tests the hazard after short-circuit; this item tests the storage-phase preventive boundary—disconnect aircraft connector and prevent terminal shorting. Flight phase plus preventive action are materially distinct.
Fire-resistant storage containment plus protection from puncture/mechanical damage is a separate storage-state proposition not covered by charge-level, swelling or post-impact LiPo items.
The explicit >35°C LiPo storage threshold is source-defined, answer-unique, and distinct from long-term charge-state management or cold-weather flight effects.
Business-use LiPo disposal as industrial waste under applicable law is an explicit end-of-life management proposition not represented by current storage/replacement items.

Tier B PASS. The winch-suspended-load branch requires reasoning about dynamic swing plus center-of-gravity change before/after release. Q073 is generic drop-device procedure and Q069 static payload CG; operation applicability and dynamics are materially distinct.

Agricultural spray-device operation within prescribed speed/altitude plus wind-drift prevention is device-specific operational-envelope knowledge distinct from general drop-device or legal-procedure questions.
